decision.scope: Do not claim a Badger-versus-KelinciWCA outcome or start the matched-CPU experiment on this machine.
decision.reason: The source repositories are pinned and the native Kelinci interface builds, but the Java/Ant/Gradle/AFL/JPF/SPF/Z3 stack and a common cost-counter implementation are not reproducibly assembled. The available container exposes CPU counters but lacks the required build tools and network access was disabled.

exact_cost.interpretation: These are bounded local feasibility costs only; they are not experiment outcomes and do not include an unperformed dependency installation.

research_question: Can the 2018 Badger hybrid claim be tested against standalone KelinciWCA using held-out Java subjects, a matched worst-case cost metric, equal CPU, and equal wall-clock budget?

hypothesis_and_competing_explanations.H1: At matched resources, Badger generates a larger maximum resource-cost input than standalone KelinciWCA on held-out Java subjects.
hypothesis_and_competing_explanations.H0_resource: The published advantage is partly or wholly caused by one KelinciWCA process plus one SymExe process versus single-core component baselines.
hypothesis_and_competing_explanations.H0_construct: Badger and KelinciWCA optimize different or differently instrumented cost constructs, so an apparent advantage is not a matched estimand.
hypothesis_and_competing_explanations.H0_subject: The result depends on the selected subjects and is not independently testable with a held-out, non-overlapping Java suite from the available checkout.

sources_and_data.observed: The paper defines KelinciWCA cost as executed conditions/branches, wall-clock timing, or user-defined costs; its threat-to-validity section states that Badger used one KelinciWCA process and one SymExe process while individual tools used one core, and calls this a possible advantage.

sources_and_data.build_contract: badger/badger/build.xml via Ant; requires JPF core, SPF, solver libraries, and a local .jpf/site.properties
fuzzerside/make plus instrumentor/build.gradle; requires AFL and Java dependencies args4j 2.32, ASM 5.2, and commons-io 2.4

sources_and_data.integrity: both repositories were clean at the recorded commits; no source files were modified

steps: Read the prior Badger feasibility and Paper 4 action-plan artifacts, then inspected the pinned repository heads, build files, dependency declarations, metric implementations, evaluation directories, and example subjects.
Ran the documented Badger Ant build, KelinciWCA Gradle build, and Kelinci native-interface Make build in disposable checkouts.
Probed host and disposable-container Java, compiler, Ant, Gradle, AFL, and Docker availability without installing packages or enabling services.
Probed cgroup-v2 cpu.stat in the pinned container and measured usage_usec before and after a bounded 0.25-second busy loop.
Separated source observations and feasibility measurements from any claim about comparative performance.
frozen_exclusions: No paid compute, package download, persistent service, full-text PDF download, or production OpenFindings change.
No Java benchmark execution, cost-counter calibration, paired randomization, or outcome measurement was attempted after the build gate failed.
The existing repository worktree changes were not touched.

independent_java_subjects.finding: The available material contains multiple subjects/examples, but it does not provide a verified held-out independent suite with a completed common build. Several names overlap or are derived from the Badger evaluation; independence and comparability therefore remain unverified.

worst_case_cost_metric.source_definition: Badger's default timing proxy is an instrumented count of executed jumps/branches; KelinciWCA also reports runtime and memory, and user-defined costs.
worst_case_cost_metric.fairness_result: No cross-arm equivalence was established. cgroup CPU time is an external resource budget, not the same thing as the input-ranking objective. A valid study must freeze one identical subject-level cost definition and independently record cgroup CPU usage.

cgroup_cpu_observability.probe: before 37793, after 300193, delta 262400 usec after a bounded busy loop
cgroup_cpu_observability.limitation: The macOS host does not expose the Linux cgroup files directly; the future experiment must run both arms inside equivalent Linux containers/cgroups and retain raw cpu.stat snapshots.

prerequisites: Build and hash a Java/Ant/JPF/SPF/Z3 environment and resolve KelinciWCA dependencies with checksums.
Build the repository's AFL fork, KelinciWCA instrumentor, Badger, and the same instrumented subject successfully.
Demonstrate that both arms emit the same subject-level cost for a fixed calibration input, while separately logging cgroup CPU usage.
Predeclare a non-overlapping subject set and verify each subject runs deterministically on the pinned JDK.
resource_fairness_protocol_if_reopened.allocation: One Linux cgroup per arm, one CPU effective quota per cgroup, same memory limit, same JDK/container digest, equal usage_usec stopping target, randomized arm order within subject/seed, and no shared concurrent host workload.
resource_fairness_protocol_if_reopened.primary_metric: Maximum verified common cost observed per subject and seed at the equal cgroup usage_usec target; do not substitute wall time or raw process count.
resource_fairness_protocol_if_reopened.falsification_gate: If any subject cannot produce identical calibration costs, if either arm lacks complete raw CPU counters, or if the subject suite is not independent and held out, the matched-CPU claim is falsified as a measurement design and the experiment stops.

uncertainty: The exact Java version compatible with the 2018 JPF/SPF fork was not resolved; JDK 21 compatibility is unknown.
JPF core, SPF, Z3, AFL, and Gradle/Ant dependency artifacts were not built or checksum-pinned in this session.
No independent held-out subject set was authenticated.
The cgroup observation is container-local and demonstrates instrumentation availability, not end-to-end Badger/KelinciWCA CPU fairness.
No performance outcome, null outcome, bug yield, or comparative scientific result was observed.

next_falsifiable_action.action: Acquire or construct a finite, offline, checksum-pinned Linux build image containing a Java version compatible with the pinned JPF/SPF code, Ant, Gradle, AFL fork, Z3, and all declared jars; then run only a one-subject calibration gate.
next_falsifiable_action.pass_condition: Both standalone KelinciWCA and Badger complete the same calibration subject, produce the same frozen cost metric on fixed inputs, and expose raw cgroup usage_usec counters.
next_falsifiable_action.fail_condition: Any missing dependency, incompatible build, metric mismatch, absent counter, nondeterministic fixed-input cost, or lack of an independent subject causes a no-go without comparative outcome claims.

claims_not_supported: This artifact does not reproduce the Badger paper's result.
This artifact does not establish that Badger is better or worse than KelinciWCA.
The planning information-gain estimate of 0.65 remains unvalidated.
